There are several ways to run MSTest tests depending on your needs. You can run tests from an IDE (for example, Visual Studio, Visual Studio Code, or JetBrains Rider), or from the command line, or from a CI service (such as GitHub Actions or Azure DevOps).

Historically, MSTest relied on [VSTest](https://github.com/microsoft/vstest) for running tests in all contexts but starting with version 3.2.0, MSTest has its own test runner. This new runner is more lightweight and faster than VSTest, and it's the recommended way to run MSTest tests.

## VSTest vs MTP

MSTest supports running tests with both VSTest and [Microsoft.Testing.Platform (MTP)](microsoft-testing-platform-intro). This extension provides a compatibility layer with VSTest allowing test frameworks that are already implemented with VSTest to:

*   Run easily with Microsoft.Testing.Platform (MTP) without a major rewrite.
*   Support both VSTest and MTP with the same test framework implementation.

This extension is shipped as part of [Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.VSTestBridge](https://nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.VSTestBridge) NuGet package.

## Compatibility with VSTest

The main purpose of this extension is to offer an easy and smooth upgrade experience for VSTest users by allowing a dual mode where the new platform is enabled and in parallel a compatibility mode is offered to allow the usual workflows to continue working.

## Runsettings support

This extension allows you to provide a [VSTest _.runsettings_ file](/en-us/visualstudio/test/configure-unit-tests-by-using-a-dot-runsettings-file), but not all options in this file are picked up by the platform. We describe below the supported and unsupported settings, configuration options and alternatives for the most used VSTest configuration options.

When enabled by the test framework, you can use `--settings <SETTINGS_FILE>` to provide the `.runsettings` file.

### RunConfiguration element

The following **RunConfiguration** elements are not supported by MTP:

Node

Description

Reason / Workaround

**MaxCpuCount**

This setting controls the level of parallelism on process-level. Use 0 to enable the maximum process-level parallelism.

When MTP is used with MSBuild, this option is [offloaded to MSBuild](/en-us/visualstudio/msbuild/building-multiple-projects-in-parallel-with-msbuild). When a single executable is run, this option has no meaning for MTP.

**ResultsDirectory**

The directory where test results are placed. The path is relative to the directory that contains the _.runsettings_ file.

Use the command-line option `--results-directory` to determine the directory where the test results are going to be placed. If the specified directory doesn't exist, it's created. The default is `TestResults` in the directory that contains the test application.

**TargetFrameworkVersion**

This setting defines the framework version, or framework family to use to run tests.

This option is ignored. The `<TargetFramework>` or `<TargetFrameworks>` MSBuild properties determine the target framework of the application. The tests are hosted in the final application.

**TargetPlatform**

This setting defines the architecture to use to run tests.

`<RuntimeIdentifier>` determines the architecture of the final application that hosts the tests.

**TreatTestAdapterErrorsAsWarnings**

Suppresses test adapter errors to become warnings.

MTP allows only one type of tests to be run from a single assembly, and failure to load the test framework or other parts of infrastructure will become an un-skippable error, because it signifies that some tests could not be discovered or run.

**TestAdaptersPaths**

One or more paths to the directory where the TestAdapters are located

MTP does not use the concept of test adapters and does not allow dynamic loading of extensions unless they are part of the build, and are registered in `Program.cs`, either automatically via build targets or manually.

**TestCaseFilter**

A filter to limit tests which will run.

Starting with v1.6, this runsettings entry is now supported. Before this version, you should use `--filter` command line option instead.

**TestSessionTimeout**

Allows users to terminate a test session when it exceeds a given timeout.

There is no alternative option.

**DotnetHostPath**

Specify a custom path to dotnet host that is used to run the test host.

MTP is not doing any additional resolving of dotnet. It depends fully on how dotnet resolves itself, which can be controlled by environment variables such as [`DOTNET_HOST_PATH`](../tools/dotnet-environment-variables#dotnet_host_path).

**TreatNoTestsAsError**

Exit with non-zero exit code when no tests are discovered.

MTP will error by default when no tests are discovered or run in a test application. You can set how many tests you expect to find in the assembly by using `--minimum-expected-tests` command line parameter, which defaults to 1.

### DataCollectors element

MTP is not using data collectors. Instead it has the concept of in-process and out-of-process extensions. Each extension is configured by its respective configuration file or through the command line.

Most importantly [hang](microsoft-testing-platform-crash-hang-dumps#hang-dump) and [crash](microsoft-testing-platform-crash-hang-dumps#crash-dump) extension, and [code coverage](microsoft-testing-platform-code-coverage) extension.

### LoggerRunSettings element

Loggers in MTP are configured through command-line parameters or by settings in code.

## VSTest filter support

This extension also offer the ability to use VSTest filtering mechanism to discover or run only the tests that matches the filter expression. For more information, see the [Filter option details](../tools/dotnet-test-vstest#filter-option-details) section or for framework specific details see the [Running selective unit tests](selective-unit-tests) page.

When enabled by the test framework, you can use `--filter <FILTER_EXPRESSION>`.

## TestRun parameters

You can pass parameters to the test run by using the `--test-parameter` command line option in the format `key=value`. This option can be specified multiple times, one for each parameter to set.

These parameters can then be accessed by the test framework in the test run:

*   for MSTest, use [Properties](/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.visualstudio.testtools.unittesting.testcontext.properties#microsoft-visualstudio-testtools-unittesting-testcontext-properties)
*   for NUnit, use [TestContext.TestParameters](https://docs.nunit.org/articles/nunit/writing-tests/TestContext.html#testparameters)

This extension is shipped as part of [Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.VSTestBridge](https://nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.VSTestBridge) NuGet package.

## Compatibility with VSTest

The main purpose of this extension is to offer an easy and smooth upgrade experience for VSTest users by allowing a dual mode where the new platform is enabled and in parallel a compatibility mode is offered to allow the usual workflows to continue working.

## Runsettings support

This extension allows you to provide a [VSTest _.runsettings_ file](/en-us/visualstudio/test/configure-unit-tests-by-using-a-dot-runsettings-file), but not all options in this file are picked up by the platform. We describe below the supported and unsupported settings, configuration options and alternatives for the most used VSTest configuration options.

When enabled by the test framework, you can use `--settings <SETTINGS_FILE>` to provide the `.runsettings` file.

### RunConfiguration element

The following **RunConfiguration** elements are not supported by MTP:

Node

Description

Reason / Workaround

**MaxCpuCount**

This setting controls the level of parallelism on process-level. Use 0 to enable the maximum process-level parallelism.

When MTP is used with MSBuild, this option is [offloaded to MSBuild](/en-us/visualstudio/msbuild/building-multiple-projects-in-parallel-with-msbuild). When a single executable is run, this option has no meaning for MTP.

**ResultsDirectory**

The directory where test results are placed. The path is relative to the directory that contains the _.runsettings_ file.

Use the command-line option `--results-directory` to determine the directory where the test results are going to be placed. If the specified directory doesn't exist, it's created. The default is `TestResults` in the directory that contains the test application.

**TargetFrameworkVersion**

This setting defines the framework version, or framework family to use to run tests.

This option is ignored. The `<TargetFramework>` or `<TargetFrameworks>` MSBuild properties determine the target framework of the application. The tests are hosted in the final application.

**TargetPlatform**

This setting defines the architecture to use to run tests.

`<RuntimeIdentifier>` determines the architecture of the final application that hosts the tests.

**TreatTestAdapterErrorsAsWarnings**

Suppresses test adapter errors to become warnings.

MTP allows only one type of tests to be run from a single assembly, and failure to load the test framework or other parts of infrastructure will become an un-skippable error, because it signifies that some tests could not be discovered or run.

**TestAdaptersPaths**

One or more paths to the directory where the TestAdapters are located

MTP does not use the concept of test adapters and does not allow dynamic loading of extensions unless they are part of the build, and are registered in `Program.cs`, either automatically via build targets or manually.

**TestCaseFilter**

A filter to limit tests which will run.

Starting with v1.6, this runsettings entry is now supported. Before this version, you should use `--filter` command line option instead.

**TestSessionTimeout**

Allows users to terminate a test session when it exceeds a given timeout.

There is no alternative option.

**DotnetHostPath**

Specify a custom path to dotnet host that is used to run the test host.

MTP is not doing any additional resolving of dotnet. It depends fully on how dotnet resolves itself, which can be controlled by environment variables such as [`DOTNET_HOST_PATH`](../tools/dotnet-environment-variables#dotnet_host_path).

**TreatNoTestsAsError**

Exit with non-zero exit code when no tests are discovered.

MTP will error by default when no tests are discovered or run in a test application. You can set how many tests you expect to find in the assembly by using `--minimum-expected-tests` command line parameter, which defaults to 1.

### DataCollectors element

MTP is not using data collectors. Instead it has the concept of in-process and out-of-process extensions. Each extension is configured by its respective configuration file or through the command line.

Most importantly [hang](microsoft-testing-platform-crash-hang-dumps#hang-dump) and [crash](microsoft-testing-platform-crash-hang-dumps#crash-dump) extension, and [code coverage](microsoft-testing-platform-code-coverage) extension.

### LoggerRunSettings element

Loggers in MTP are configured through command-line parameters or by settings in code.

## VSTest filter support

This extension also offer the ability to use VSTest filtering mechanism to discover or run only the tests that matches the filter expression. For more information, see the [Filter option details](../tools/dotnet-test-vstest#filter-option-details) section or for framework specific details see the [Running selective unit tests](selective-unit-tests) page.

When enabled by the test framework, you can use `--filter <FILTER_EXPRESSION>`.

## TestRun parameters

You can pass parameters to the test run by using the `--test-parameter` command line option in the format `key=value`. This option can be specified multiple times, one for each parameter to set.

These parameters can then be accessed by the test framework in the test run:

*   for MSTest, use [Properties](/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.visualstudio.testtools.unittesting.testcontext.properties#microsoft-visualstudio-testtools-unittesting-testcontext-properties)

# Migration Plan: VSTest → Microsoft.Testing.Platform (MTP)

## Problem
5 MSTest projects currently use VSTest (`MSTest.TestFramework` + `MSTest.TestAdapter` + `Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk` all at 3.8.0/17.13.0). CI uses Azure DevOps `VSTest@3` task with TRX reporting and code coverage. Goal: migrate to Microsoft.Testing.Platform runner.

## Approach
Use the **MSTest meta-package** (`MSTest 4.1.0`) which bundles everything including TRX and code-coverage extensions. Enable MTP via `EnableMSTestRunner`. Replace `VSTest@3` in Azure DevOps with `DotNetCoreCLI@2` (`dotnet test`).

---

## Phase 1 – Prepare (solution-wide props)

### 1.1 Add/update `Directory.Build.props` in the solution root
```xml
<Project>
  <PropertyGroup>
    <!-- Enable Microsoft.Testing.Platform runner -->
    <EnableMSTestRunner>true</EnableMSTestRunner>

    <!-- Required: MTP test projects compile as executables -->
    <OutputType>Exe</OutputType>

    <!-- Let `dotnet test` discover MTP-based projects -->
    <TestingPlatformDotnetTestSupport>true</TestingPlatformDotnetTestSupport>

    <!-- Show per-test failures on console (slight perf cost) -->
    <TestingPlatformShowTestsFailure>true</TestingPlatformShowTestsFailure>
  </PropertyGroup>
</Project>
```

### 1.2 Update each test `.csproj` – replace 3 packages with 1
**Remove:**
```xml
<PackageReference Include="MSTest.TestFramework" Version="3.8.0" />
<PackageReference Include="MSTest.TestAdapter" Version="3.8.0" />
<PackageReference Include="Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk" Version="17.13.0" />
```

**Replace with:**
```xml
<PackageReference Include="MSTest" Version="4.1.0" />
```

The `MSTest` 4.1.0 meta-package transitively includes:
- `Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk`
- `MSTest.TestFramework`
- `MSTest.TestAdapter`
- `MSTest.Analyzers`
- `Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.TrxReport`
- `Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.CodeCoverage`

> **Alternative (MSTest.Sdk):** If all 5 projects use `Microsoft.NET.Sdk` (not `.Web`), you can replace the SDK attribute instead:
> ```xml
> <Project Sdk="MSTest.Sdk/4.1.0">
> ```
> This enables MTP by default and removes the need for `EnableMSTestRunner`, `OutputType`, and the `MSTest` package reference. Projects requiring `Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web` cannot use this approach.

### 1.3 Source code changes
- **None required.** `Microsoft.VisualStudio.TestTools.UnitTesting` namespace, `[TestClass]`, `[TestMethod]`, `[TestCategory]`, etc. are unchanged.
- If you have a custom `Program.cs` or `Main` entry point in any test project, remove it — MTP auto-generates one.

---

## Phase 2 – Validate locally

### 2.1 Restore & build
```bash
dotnet restore
dotnet build --no-restore
```

### 2.2 Run tests via `dotnet test`
```bash
dotnet test --no-build
```

### 2.3 Verify TRX output
```bash
dotnet test --no-build -- --report-trx --report-trx-filename TestResults.trx
```
TRX files land in `<project>/TestResults/`.

### 2.4 Verify code coverage
```bash
dotnet test --no-build -- --coverage --coverage-output-format cobertura
```

### 2.5 Verify filters still work
```bash
dotnet test --no-build --filter "TestCategory=Slow"
```

### 2.6 Verify .runsettings (if used)
```bash
dotnet test --no-build -- --settings my.runsettings
```

---

## Phase 3 – Azure DevOps pipeline changes

### 3.1 Replace `VSTest@3` with `DotNetCoreCLI@2`

**Before (VSTest@3):**
```yaml
- task: VSTest@3
  inputs:
    testSelector: 'testAssemblies'
    testAssemblyVer2: '**/*Tests.dll'
    codeCoverageEnabled: true
    testRunTitle: 'Unit Tests'
```

**After (DotNetCoreCLI@2):**
```yaml
- task: DotNetCoreCLI@2
  displayName: 'Run tests'
  inputs:
    command: 'test'
    projects: '**/*Tests.csproj'
    arguments: >-
      --configuration Release
      --no-build
      --
      --report-trx --report-trx-filename TestResults.trx
      --coverage --coverage-output-format cobertura
```

### 3.2 Publish TRX results
```yaml
- task: PublishTestResults@2
  displayName: 'Publish test results'
  inputs:
    testResultsFormat: 'VSTest'   # TRX format = VSTest
    testResultsFiles: '**/TestResults/*.trx'
    mergeTestResults: true
    testRunTitle: 'Unit Tests'
  condition: always()
```

### 3.3 Publish code coverage
```yaml
- task: PublishCodeCoverageResults@2
  displayName: 'Publish code coverage'
  inputs:
    summaryFileLocation: '**/TestResults/**/*.cobertura.xml'
  condition: always()
```

---

## Phase 4 – Cleanup & hardening

### 4.1 Remove stale VSTest artifacts
- Delete any `*.runsettings` entries that reference `<DataCollectors>` for code coverage (MTP uses CLI flags, not data collectors). Keep `<MSTest>` and `<RunConfiguration>` sections that are still supported.
- Remove references to `vstest.console.exe` from scripts.

### 4.2 Known behavioral differences
| Area | VSTest | MTP |
|---|---|---|
| No-tests-found | Warning | **Error** (exit code 8). Use `--minimum-expected-tests 0` to suppress. |
| MaxCpuCount | runsettings | Controlled by MSBuild `/m` parallelism. |
| Code coverage default | Includes test assembly | **Excludes test assembly** by default. |
| DataCollectors | Supported | Not supported — use in-/out-of-process extensions. |

### 4.3 Optional: Enable crash/hang dump collection
```bash
dotnet test -- --crashdump --hangdump --hangdump-timeout 5m
```

---

## Todos

1. Add `Directory.Build.props` with MTP properties
2. Update `.csproj` files (replace 3 packages → `MSTest 4.1.0`)
3. Build and run tests locally
4. Verify TRX + code coverage output locally
5. Update Azure DevOps pipeline YAML
6. Run pipeline and verify test results + coverage tabs
7. Clean up deprecated runsettings / VSTest references

## Notes
- No source-code changes needed — MSTest attributes/assertions are identical.
- `dotnet test` still works; MTP is the underlying runner, not a separate CLI.
- If any project uses `Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web`, use the manual approach (not `MSTest.Sdk`).
- MSTest 4.x includes analyzers by default — expect new warnings on first build. Treat as informational and fix incrementally.

    <EnableMSTestRunner>true</EnableMSTestRunner>

    <OutputType>Exe</OutputType>

    <!-- Let `dotnet test` discover MTP-based projects -->
    <TestingPlatformDotnetTestSupport>true</TestingPlatformDotnetTestSupport>
